tier_reason: First-party (Google, 2008) benchmark page with walltime table against local_01 builds; harness code is public (bench/benchmark.py, bench/ProjectDefs.py) and CPU models are stated, but compiler version and flags are not, so it falls short of A.

corrections.caveats: First-party Google/distcc page dated 2008 (copyright line) on 2008-era hardware. The harness is in the repo (bench/benchmark.py, Build.py, compiler.py, ProjectDefs.py: exact project tarballs plus configure/build commands, compiler invoked as cc/gcc through a masquerade script farm), but no compiler version or CFLAGS are stated anywhere, so not tier A. The local baseline is one 2.8GHz Pentium 4 client against 152 server CPUs, which inflates the ratio; the page itself says a multi-processor client would show smaller gains. Only make time is counted, not configure. The page notes pump runs that silently fell back to plain mode while collecting results. The ratios above marked derived are computed from the page's wall-time column. README.md separately claims three machines are 2.6 times faster than one and README.pump says pump mode can distribute compilations up to 10X faster than plain distcc (compile step, not whole build); neither number is on the benchmark page. No comparison with ccache, icecream or a modern build system.

notes: All walltime numbers and derived ratios match doc/web/benchmark.html; README 2.6x and README.pump 10X quotes confirmed. gh CLI blocked in cloud session; metadata from github.com pages (2.3k stars, last commit 2026-07-08, GPL v2-or-later per source headers).

tier_reason: First-party BENCH file with results against make without icecream; no scripts, compiler version or flags, only a CPU model (1.7GHz Pentium M), so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Linux 2.6.16: 315s local (make -j1) vs 230s with icecream over WLAN (make -j10, about 1.37x, derived from page data) and 203s over 100MBit LAN (make -j10/100, about 1.55x, derived from page data); the file says the maximum improvement is 27% (LAN: 36%) out of a theoretical 50%. Qt 3.3.6 src/: 368s local (make -j1) vs 269s over WLAN (make -j10, about 1.37x, derived) and 239s over LAN (make -j10/100, about 1.54x, derived). Stock icecream 0.7 on the same Qt test: 349s WLAN (the file calls it a 6% speedup over local) and 253s LAN. Later note in the file (test project not named): remote with -m 1 at 0.8.0 took 257s for make -j5, and 442s without compression. Overhead of the wrapper without a cluster is about 2%.
corrections.caveats: First-party BENCH file with results only, not scripts: no compiler version or flags, no CPU beyond 1.7GHz Pentium M, circa 2006 (mentions a 2006-06-16 branch) on a two-node cluster, much older than current icecream. The cluster has only two nodes, so the 27-36% gains are bounded by a theoretical 50%. The headline rows are for development patches ('dirk's no-latency' patch, 'make-it-cool' branch), not a release; stock 0.7 gained only 6% over local on WLAN. The make -j1 local baseline is the fastest local setting for Linux (-j10 local was 334s); for Qt, local -j3 was 363s. No measured comparison against distcc anywhere in the repo; the distcc comparison in README is qualitative. Percentages are quoted from the file's own text.

notes: All quoted numbers match BENCH. Added stock-0.7 rows and derived ratios. gh CLI blocked; metadata from github.com pages (1.8k stars, last commit 2026-03-04, GPL v2-or-later per daemon/main.cpp header).
